Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Systems Engineer Co-op to join our rapidly growing team. In this role, you'll get hands-on exposure to how Anduril develops technical strategy and executes complex, integrated hardware and software programs — from pre-award demonstrations through early contract phases and full execution. You'll support a multi-disciplinary engineering team working toward efficient development and delivery of solutions for our customers.

You'll gain exposure to how systems engineering spans company boundaries in an agile, CI/CD-oriented development approach, balancing the development of new capabilities with the integration of existing Anduril technologies. You'll also see firsthand how technical status gets communicated to customers and leadership throughout a program's lifecycle.

Systems Engineering at Anduril touches every phase of program execution — from proposals through design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), qualification testing, and delivery — and spans disciplines including mechanical, thermal, structural, electrical, software, firmware, GNC, reliability, and manufacturing (integration and test). A strong Systems Engineer Co-op is someone who's technically curious across disciplines and eager to learn how these pieces fit together across a program's full lifecycle.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will own one or more scoped projects end to end, with mentor support, over the engagement. Candidate projects include:

- Trade study support — Perform a system-level trade study balancing risk, cost, and performance for a defined design decision. Deliverable: trade study writeup and recommendation reviewed by the engineering team.

- Requirements decomposition exercise — Take a defined complex system requirement and decompose it into executable sub-requirements, under mentor guidance. Deliverable: requirements decomposition document validated against an existing design.

- Design review support — Prepare supporting technical materials for an upcoming design review (SRR, PDR, or CDR) for a defined subsystem. Deliverable: review package contribution and follow-up action summary.

- Test planning support — Support the development of qualification or acceptance test requirements and pass/fail criteria for a defined component, including coordination with a vendor or subsystem owner. Deliverable: test plan contribution and results summary.

- Cross-disciplinary integration project — Work with engineers across two or more disciplines (e.g., mechanical and software) to support integration of a defined subsystem. Deliverable: integrated subsystem passing checkout, plus a summary of cross-team tradeoffs.

- Technical briefing development — Support the development of a technical briefing or status update communicating program progress to internal stakeholders. Deliverable: reviewed briefing materials used in an actual program review.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.

Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Search AI teams within Facebook. Facebook Search helps people find the people, groups, events, videos and posts they are looking for, across one of the largest and fastest-changing content collections in the world. Our teams build AI that helps people decide what to search for and find useful results. This spans personalized query suggestions before and during a search, suggested queries on Reels, and retrieval and ranking of relevant content. We bring together generative AI, multimodal understanding, and personalization to help people express intent, act on curiosity, and discover useful content at Facebook scale. Our interns will have the opportunity to frame practical, high-impact search problems as rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance of our research scientists and software engineers.

The central research challenge is to connect what a person wants to explore with content that makes the journey worthwhile. For example, a video can spark curiosity before someone has a query in mind; the system must suggest a useful question and deliver results that reward that curiosity. Models must understand explicit queries or infer interests from multimodal content, generate useful suggestions or retrieve relevant results, and balance engagement with relevance, groundedness, and factuality within strict latency and compute constraints. Open problems include generative retrieval using learned identifiers that represent content, personalized query generation, sequence models for ranking individual results and composing a useful results page, and joint learning across suggestions and results. LLM-based supervision, post-training, and online experiments help us connect model improvements to useful exploration and sustained search habits.

If you are excited about helping billions of people turn curiosity into useful discovery, from the first search suggestion to the results that follow, come join us!

Analyze and improve the efficiency, latency, scalability, and stability of models in production serving. Collaborate with researchers and cross-functional partners including communicating research plans, progress, and results.
